facts.fact: The education ministry inaugurated a modernised State Exam grading centre in Kinshasa on 10 April 2025 running the AI-using software Snote Manager to process test items.

PATH, with the Ministry of Health, piloted SnapiForm, an AI tool reading paper health registers into DHIS2, in 12 DRC health zones for several months; PATH reports reporting time fell from over two hours to about 15 minutes.

systems.owner: PATH (MACEPA) with the Ministry of Health

facts.fact: Education minister Raissa Malu told the Council of Ministers on 15 August 2025 that an AI system automated exam-paper marking in 2025, with results published three days after the exams.
Minister Malu reported AI exam processing cut processing time by 30-40 percent, raised speed tenfold, and lifted scanning from 8-10 to 80-100 papers a minute.

MINEDU-NC reports the education ministry's locally developed automated, AI-based correction of State Examination papers was demonstrated at CASP 2025 in Kinshasa on 17 December 2025, with inspectors keeping the decision role.
MINEDU-NC says the new AI correction solution processes 80 to 100 copies a minute, against 8 to 10 for the old system.

systems.owner: Ministry of National Education and New Citizenship

facts.fact: The Ministry of National Education press release says AI is integrated into State Exam grading at the National Grading Center in Kinshasa (inaugurated 10 April 2025) and at the Lubumbashi branch, which is operational and equipped to process more than 100,000 answer sheets, with Mbuji-Mayi as a second pilot centre.
